title: Palisades (Holtec restart): OEDO-26-02609 2.206 Petition - Palisades Refueling Operations - Alan Blind - NRC Screening Email (EPID L-2026-CRS-0005) [['E-Mail']]

documents.text:
From:              Dennis Galvin
To:                "Alan Blind"
Cc:                Petition Resource
Subject:           Screening of 10/4/2026 2.206 Submittal Regarding Palisades Refueling Operations
Date:              Thursday, October 29, 2026 3:37:00 PM


Hello Mr. Blind,

By email dated October 4, 2026 (Agencywide Documents Access and Management
System (ADAMS) Accession No. ML26278A197), you submitted a petition to the Nuclear
Regulatory Commission (NRC) for consideration under Title 10 of the Code of Federal
Regulations (10 CFR) 2.206. The submission requested various enforcement actions
against Palisades Energy, LLC (the licensee) regarding the Palisades Nuclear Plant (PNP
or Palisades). The NRC staff initiated its screening process in accordance with NRC
Management Directive (MD) 8.11, “Review Process for 10 CFR 2.206 Petitions,” and its
associated Directive Handbook (DH) 8.11 Section II.A.2(d) (ML18296A043). The petition is
related to the unplanned tilting of a fuel assembly during refueling operations at Palisades.

Requested Actions

The petition requests actions in three different sections of the petition, (1) I. Request for
Enforcement Action, (2) X. Request for Immediate Action, (3) XI. Conclusion. These actions
may be summarized as follows

   1. Issue a Confirmatory Order prohibiting Palisades Energy, LLC from resuming reactor
       core refueling operations without prior NRC authorization, pending
       a. NRC determination that
            1. the cause and extent of condition have been determined,
            2. corrective actions necessary to preclude recurrence have been completed,
            3. the potential contribution of fatigue and human-performance factors has
                   been evaluated,
             4. the Fuel Handling System can safely perform its FSAR [final safety analysis
                   report] -described design function
       b. NRC independent verification of the adequacy of the applicable 10 CFR 50.59
           review.

   2. Suspend the August 12, 2026 [ML26216A290], exemption from the normal work-hour
       requirements of 10 CFR 26.205(d)(3) and (d)(7), as applicable to Operations
       personnel participating in reactor core refueling activities, pending NRC determination
       of whether
              a. fatigue or human-performance factors caused or contributed to the event,
              b. the basis for NRC's reasonable-assurance finding remains valid.

   3. If substantive deficiencies are identified in the Refueling Machine modification or its
       10 CFR 50.59 review, initiate an Event and Causal Factors Inspection, Special
       Inspection, or other appropriate focused inspection to determine whether those
      deficiencies have broader applicability to the Palisades restart modification program.

Basis for Request

Most of the petition discusses requests for NRC inspection and evaluations, which are not
enforcement actions, and therefore, are not applicable to the 2.206 process. Requests for
NRC inspections and evaluations are also not considered a basis for the requested
enforcement actions.

The petition cites 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix B, Criterion XVI, “Corrective Action,” and 10
CFR 50.59, “Changes, tests, and experiments,” as applicable to the petition. Criterion XVI
requires the following.

       Measures shall be established to assure that conditions adverse to quality, such as
       failures, malfunctions, deficiencies, deviations, defective material and equipment,
       and nonconformances are promptly identified and corrected. In the case of
       significant conditions adverse to quality, the measures shall assure that the cause of
       the condition is determined and corrective action taken to preclude repetition. The
       identification of the significant condition adverse to quality, the cause of the
       condition, and the corrective action taken shall be documented and reported to
       appropriate levels of management.

The regulations in 10 CFR 50.59(c)(1) permit a licensee to make changes in the facility as
described in the final safety analysis report if the change does not meet any of the criteria in
10 CFR 50.59(c)(2).

The petition does not assert that either regulation has been violated. While the direct
causes of an event may need to be remedied to restore a system to operation, more
systemic causes may need to be evaluated concurrent with restored operations to prevent
long-term repetition of events. Criterion XVI does not require the suspension of reactor
operations if a condition adverse to quality is identified, though suspension of certain
system operations or reactor operations may occur if the condition adverse to quality
results in certain limiting conditions for operation in the technical specifications not to be
met. Rather, Criterion XVI requires licensees to have a program to address conditions
adverse to quality. Criterion XVI also does not require the NRC confirmation of all of a
licensee’s corrective actions. NRC actions are governed by its inspection program, which is
conducted on a sampling basis.

Screening Evaluation

The NRC staff has screened your request out of the 2.206 petition process consistent with
MD 8.11, DH Section II.A.2(d)(v), “Requests That Would Not Reasonably Lead to an
Enforcement Action,” and MD 8.11, DH Section II.A.2(d)(ii)(2) “A General Assertion Without
Supporting Facts.”

Prohibition of the Resumption of Refueling Operations

As discussed above, the request to prohibit the resumption of refueling operations after the
recovery of the tilted fuel assembly does not assert a violation of the regulations. The
 petition does not assert that the licensee has not implemented its corrective action
program. Criterion XVI does not require the suspension of reactor operations when an item
is entered into the corrective action program. Therefore, the petition does not provide a
basis to prohibit the resumption of refueling operations after the recovery of the tilted fuel
assembly. Based on the forgoing, the request to prohibit the resumption of refueling
operations after the recovery of the tilted fuel assembly is a request that would not
reasonably lead to an enforcement action and therefore, screens out in accordance with
MD 8.11, DH Section II.A.2(d)(v).

Suspension of Work-Hour Exemption

The petitioner requests the suspension of the August 12, 2026, exemption that modifies
certain work-hour requirements, but the petition does not provide any basis for the
suspension. Specifically, the petition states in Section VIII, “NRC Work-Hour Exemption
and Potential Role of Fatigue and Human Performance,” Subsection C, “Significance of the
Subsequent Fuel-Assembly Tilting Event”:

       The petitioner does not assert, based upon presently available information, that
       fatigue caused the event.

Further, the petition does not assert the inadequacy of the approved exemption. A
speculation that fatigue resulting from the exemption modified work hour requirements
could have contributed to the tipped over fuel assembly event is not a statement of facts.
Based on the request for the suspension of the work-hour exemption being a general
assertion without supporting facts, the request screens out in accordance with MD 8.11,
DH Section II.A.2(d)(ii)(2).

50.59 Review of the Fuel Handling System Modification

The petitioner requests the NRC independent verification of the adequacy of the applicable
10 CFR 50.59 review for the fuel handling system, but the petition does not provide any
basis for the request. In Section II, “Regulatory Requirements at Issue,” Subsection B, “10
CFR 50.59 — Recently Modified Fuel Handling System,” the petition states regarding the
modification of fuel handling system:

       The petitioner does not presently assert that the licensee's 10 CFR 50.59 evaluation
       was inadequate.

Beyond a request for additional NRC inspections being of out scope for the 2.206 process,
the petition does not provide any basis for the request. The purpose of a 10 CFR 50.59
evaluation is to determine whether a particular change requires prior NRC approval, which
is unrelated to the adequacy of the change or an event. The petition does not assert that
the modification of the fuel handling system required prior NRC approval or was
inadequate. A speculation that the modified fuel handling system could have contributed to
the tipped over fuel assembly event is not a statement of facts. Based on any implied
assertion regarding the fuel handling system being a general assertion without supporting
facts, any implied request related to the fuel handling system screens out in accordance
with MD 8.11, DH Section II.A.2(d)(ii)(2).

Other System Modifications
 The petitioner requests NRC to review other system modifications depending on the results
of a review of the 10 CFR 50.59 evaluation of the fuel handling system. In Section VI, “NRC
Review of the Refueling Machine Modification and 10 CFR 50.59 Evaluation,” Subsection
A, “Broader 10 CFR 50.59 Inspection if Findings Are Identified,” the petition states
regarding the modification of fuel handling system:

       The petitioner does not assert that §50.59 deficiencies exist in those other
       modifications.

Beyond a request for additional NRC inspections being out scope for the 2.206 process, the
petition does not provide any basis for the request. The petition does not assert that the
modifications of other systems required prior NRC approval or were inadequate. A
speculation that the deficiencies in one system or its documentation implies deficiencies in
unrelated systems or their documentation is not a statement of facts. Based on any implied
assertion regarding the modifications of other systems being a general assertion without
supporting facts, any implied request related to the other system modifications screens out
in accordance with MD 8.11, DH Section II.A.2(d)(ii)(2).

NRC Authorization of Alternative Fuel Handling Method

During the planning of the recovery operations of the tilted fuel assembly, the licensee
determined that damage to the upper tie plate of the tilted fuel assembly prevented the
handling of the tilted fuel assembly as described in the Palisades Updated Final Safety
Analysis Report (UFSAR). Accordingly, the licensee determined that the use of an alternate
fuel handling method required prior NRC approval. By letter dated September 30, 2026
(ML26273A469), as supplemented by letters dated October 2, 2026, October 8, 2026, and
October 12, 2026 (ML26275A214, ML26281A333, and ML26285A034, respectively), the
licensee submitted a license amendment request. By letter dated October 13, 2026
(ML26282A040), the NRC authorized the amendment while documenting the NRC
consideration of the following:

      Change to UFSAR Section 9.11, Fuel Handling and Storage Systems
      Potential Fuel Handling Accident
      Movement of the Fuel Assembly Outside of the Reactor Cavity or Spent Fuel Pool
      Recovery Equipment
      Fuel Bundle Integrity During Planned Move

The NRC concluded that (1) there is reasonable assurance that the health and safety of the
public will not be endangered by operation in the proposed manner, (2) there is reasonable
assurance that such activities will be conducted in compliance with the Commission’s
regulations, and (3) the issuance of the amendment will not be inimical to the common
defense and security or to the health and safety of the public.

Discussion of Requested and Actual Inspection Program

The petition in effect proposes an alternative inspection program following the tipped over
fuel assembly event in contrast to the actual inspection program. Request for NRC actions,
such as an alternate inspection program, are outside the scope of the 10 CFR 2.206
 process.

It merits noting that the NRC has implemented its inspection program to respond to the
tipped over fuel assembly event and is continuing to do so. NRC inspectors are utilizing
several baseline inspection procedures and a manual chapter as part of this response,
which may be accessed via the inspection manual https://www.nrc.gov/regulations-
legislation/inspection-manual.

      IP 71153, “Follow-up of Events and Notices of Enforcement Discretion” is being used
      to evaluate the licensee event and degraded conditions for plant status and mitigating
      actions. The procedure includes evaluating whether the licensee has appropriately
      resolved event issues before restart, where applicable.
      IP 71111.20, “Refueling and Other Outage Activities,” is being used in part to verify
      that reactor core refueling activities are appropriately conducted.
      IP 71152, “Problem Identification and Resolution,” is being used to follow the
      licensee’s root cause evaluation process for this issue. This process will identify the
      root and contributing causes of the event and identify corrective actions that need to
      be implemented prior to moving fuel again. The inspectors ensure these corrective
      actions are implemented and appropriate.
      IMC 0309, “Reactive Inspection Decision Basis for Power Reactors,” is being used in
      conjunction with Management Directive 8.3 “NRC Incident Investigation Program,”
      dated May 4, 2023 (ML22294A067), to determine if a reactive inspection is needed.

Specific inspection activities, as applicable, will be documented in Palisades inspection
reports, which are available here https://www.nrc.gov/documents-reports/inspection-
reports-operating-power-reactors#pali.

No Immediate Actions

The immediate requested actions in the petition are equivalent to requested actions listed
above, which the foregoing discussion shows screen out of the 10 CFR 2.206 process.
Therefore, the NRC staff concluded, in conjunction with reviewing the concerns in
accordance with DH Section II.B.1, that the concerns expressed in your request do not
warrant immediate enforcement action by the NRC.

Appreciation for Using the 2.206 Petition Process

Thank you for bringing these issues to the attention of the NRC. The 2.206 petition process
exists to identify safety issues at NRC licensed facilities and your efforts are appreciated.
For more information on the petition process please see https://www.nrc.gov/about-
nrc/regulatory/enforcement/petition.html.

Respectfully,

Dennis Galvin
Project Manager / Agency 2.206 Petition Coordinator
 U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission
Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation
Division of Licensing Projects I
Operating Reactor Licensing Branch 2
301-415-6256
